verdicts.summary: The combined rev-parse is guarded by exit code and line count, and any mismatch falls back to the old separate commands. I found no input that gets past the guard with wrong values.
verdicts.scenario: I tried four cases. (1) A common dir containing a newline: stdout has 5 lines with HEAD or 4 when unborn, which never matches the expected 4 or 3 for the exit code, so it falls back. (2) A corrupt HEAD that exits 128: it falls back to hasHeadCommit, which treats any non-zero exit as no HEAD, as before. (3) Git older than 2.31 echoing --path-format: the line count is off, so it falls back. (4) A symlinked cwd: the absolute path comes from git's physical cwd, which matches what resolveGitCommonDir produced by resolving against realPath. The call has allowNonZeroExit, so neither the darwin fsync retry (VcsProcess.ts:279-298) nor the transient-failure retry applies. The old calls did not pass env either, so worktree and GIT_INDEX_FILE behaviour is unchanged.
